title: kithd: POST /jmap/upload/{accountId} blob upload handler
description:
What: Implement the JMAP blob upload endpoint that accepts binary data, enforces size limits, stores blob, and returns blobId.

Algorithm:
1. Add route POST /jmap/upload/:account_id to build_app in kithd/src/lib.rs.
2. Handler signature: async fn blob_upload_handler(State(app): State<AppState<W>>, Extension(caller): Extension<Caller>, Path(account_id): Path<String>, request: Request) -> impl IntoResponse.
3. Verify caller.role == Role::Owner; else return 403.
4. Verify account_id == app.owner_id; else return invalidArguments 400.
5. Extract Content-Type header (optional); cap at 256 bytes; default to application/octet-stream.
6. Read request body with streaming byte count: use axum::body::to_bytes with limit of 104_857_600. Return 413 if exceeded.
7. Generate blob_id = generate_blob_id().
8. Call app.blob_store.write_blob(&blob_id, &bytes). Return 500 on failure.
9. Compute sha256 of bytes (sha2::Sha256).
10. Insert into store: store.attachments().insert_blob(&blob_id, content_type, bytes.len() as u64, &sha256, now_unix).
11. Return 201 Created with JSON: {blobId, size, type, sha256}.

Defensive rules: size limit enforced before storage; blob_id server-generated only; never trust client-supplied size; content-type stored as metadata only, not security-relevant; no secrets in logs.

Agent team: R reads existing handler patterns in kithd/src/lib.rs; I implements; T writes integration test: POST blob, verify response fields, verify blob persisted; V runs cargo test -p kithd + clippy.
